`![x\"x](x)` with smarty now gives `

`, the same as the unescaped version. **Cause:** smarty adds `"` and `'` to the backslash-escapable characters. Escaped characters are stored as placeholders and were only turned back into real characters by `UnescapePostprocessor`. That postprocessor ran *after* the document had been converted to an HTML string, so a raw `"` went straight into the `alt="..."` attribute without being escaped. **Fix:** - **`markdown/treeprocessors.py`:** new `UnescapeTreeprocessor`, registered at priority 0. It restores escaped characters in element text, tail text and attribute values *before* the HTML is written out, so the normal output escaping applies to them. It skips the text of `` elements and runs after `toc` (5) and smarty (2), so escaped quotes still aren't turned into curly quotes. - **`markdown/postprocessors.py`:** `UnescapePostprocessor` is no longer registered and is marked deprecated. One side effect: it's now a function wrapper rather than a class, so third-party code that subclasses it or uses `isinstance` on it would break. - **`docs/change_log/release-3.4.md`:** added a bug-fix entry. **Visible behaviour change:** characters that were already valid but unescaped are now HTML-escaped, e.g. `\>` now outputs `>` instead of a raw `>`. I updated `tests/basic/backlash-escapes.html` to match. **Tests:** - New `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_smarty.py`: escaped `"`/`'` in plain text, the issue's image alt case, and escaped quotes in a link title. Without the fix, the alt and title tests fail. - Added a `\>`-in-alt test to `tests/test_syntax/inline/test_images.py`. **Results:** the new and updated tests pass, and the issue example gives the right output. - The full suite (`python -m unittest discover tests`) shows 8 failures, the same 8 as before my change. They're in the raw-HTML-block tests and look like a mismatch with this Python version's HTML parser. - `pytest` can't run the whole `tests` directory because a collection error in `test_md_in_html.py` stops it, both before and after my change. Running individual files with pytest works. - I couldn't run the linter because flake8 isn't installed in `.venv`. **Not covered:** escapes in reference-style link definitions (`[ref]: x "a \"b\""`) keep their backslashes, because those definitions are read before escapes are processed. That was already the behaviour before this change, and I didn't change it. Nothing is committed.
